lead: Rheinmetall / RHM.DE — Germany is back and Europe is rearming
smaller: Ripple XRP / XRP-USD — the reserve bounce
IonQ / IONQ — the quantum dip everyone wants
Silver / SLV — the squeeze is coming
why_lead: Rheinmetall closed at 1,199.00 euros, up 19.78% over five sessions and 69.73% over 20, while the German fiscal-pivot headlines of March 3 to 5 and the rearmament coverage carried the same story. Reuters reported retail traders behind Eutelsat's 650% surge on March 6, the most explicit retail attribution in the window, and the Polish retail press calls armaments the hottest commodity on the market, so price and attention point the same way.
why_smaller: XRP is up 18.77% over five sessions on the card, and Eric Trump's 'win for retail' remark and Barron's fresh-Trump-boost piece make it the policy-driven token trade of the day.

IonQ is down 51.61% over 20 sessions on the card, and Motley Fool and Yahoo pieces frame the sell-off as a dip, while IBD ties the crash to Nvidia's chief executive and an upcoming Quantum Day, a narrative separate from AI infrastructure.

Silver is the non-equity, non-AI trade: SLV is up 4.54% over five sessions on the card, and Kitco's squeeze call and the Economist's silver-is-the-new-gold line give it an attention story that is neither defence, crypto nor quantum.
considered_not_chosen: Palantir: a 20.62% 20-session drawdown and CEO share-sale coverage, but the fan-exit and bear-ETF items read as the crowd leaving, not buying the dip, so the price and attention did not coincide.

Tesla: the largest volume of coverage and a 30.34% 20-session drop, but the coverage is about politics, protests and analyst targets rather than retail dip-buying, and the lead needs attention and price to coincide.

Nebius: a Stocktwits 'retail's elated' item on the 300MW New Jersey data centre and a 21.01% 20-session fall, but only one social item sits behind it, so it was kept out of the lead and the smaller set.
Bitcoin and ether: the Trump reserve order is the largest headline cluster, but it is already covered in the crypto section, so it was not repeated as a retail lead.
Sandisk: a Stocktwits 'retail's excited' item on a relisted name, but the card has only 15 prior observations and no 20-session return, so the new-listing rule rules it out.
TSMC: a Stocktwits 'retail remains bullish' item while the stock slid to a four-month low, but it is a mega-cap, not a speculative name, and its story sits in the semiconductor section.
Broadcom and HPE: post-earnings headlines dated 6 March conflict with the card and with after-close release timing, so no direction was used and neither was chosen.
China trade data: the exports-miss headline is dated 6 March but describes a release that may have landed after the cutoff, so it was dropped rather than used.
